body:
Note that `VSYNC_ADAPTIVE` and `VSYNC_MAILBOX` are treated as `VSYNC_ENABLED` on macOS, so I suggest checking for `vsync_mode != DisplayServer::VSYNC_DISABLED` instead.

(This also applies to the Compatibility rendering method, where adaptive and mailbox V-Sync are not supported in the OpenGL standard.)
I made the change. Thanks for the heads up!
@passivestar Did this fix it on your end?

I don't think this is related but I can check

Edit: I checked, this is unrelated. I don't use adaptive or mailbox on mac
On my end the framerate is stable with vsync enabled. Is the change in `rendering_context_driver_metal.mm` the only change you have?
If the change is regressing vsync behavior, then I think somewhere else there is a bug with how the vsync_mode value is set.

Well I just triple-checked and this is confusing, but it does regress to unstable FPS as soon as this line is put into the conditional statement:

```
[p_cmd_buffer->get_command_buffer() presentDrawable:drawable afterMinimumDuration:present_minimum_duration];
```

I tried taking it out of it myself and recompiling and I get stable 120 as soon as I do that. ~~I also did a check to make sure that the correct branch is running when it's in it, so it's not a problem with `vsync_mode` either~~

Edit: I checked both branches, it's running both of them. It mostly runs the first branch, but sometimes it runs the second one, which causes unstable fps. so `vsync_mode` variable is in fact not the same each frame
What macOS version are you using by the way? I'm testing on macOS 15.1. You might be seeing some weird Metal bug.
Thanks for confirming! So there is a separate bug that makes `vsync_mode` not stable...

@passivestar 
Are you able to track exactly when the vsync setting gets changed during runtime?

I went to check the call stack but I can't reproduce the issue anymore no matter what I do. Apparently it was something external that caused different vsync values. In any case it appears to be unrelated to this PR, I'll open another issue if I face it again

Shouldn't this branch still run if `present_minimum_duration` is greater than 0?

This seems to make it so we don't benefit from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99041 when vsync is disabled. But you are very likely to be using `max_fps` when vsync is disabled.
I see, so you are saying when vsync is disabled, but `max_fps` is set, we still expect the renderer to limit the FPS?
That's right. We actually handle that in `OS::add_frame_delay` on the CPU side. But using `afterMinimumDuration` allows us to smooth it out and time things with the screen refresh

Enabling that branch will implicitly enable vsync since macOS will limit frame rate to something the display can support.

Alternatively, you could query the refresh rate of the display and enable that branch only if the max FPS can be evenly divided by the refresh rate.
I might have just answered my own question. This probably provides no benefit when not using Vsync if the whole purpose is allowing us to synchronize better with vsync.

> Enabling that branch will implicitly enable vsync since macOS will limit frame rate to something the display can support.
> 
> Alternatively, you could query the refresh rate of the display and enable that branch only if the max FPS can be evenly divided by the refresh rate.

Thanks for your response. That makes sense. I agree we should just leave it off when not using vsync.
